squawks.headline: Japan corporate services prices rise 3.7% y/y in September
squawks.detail: Data published on Tuesday show Japan's corporate services price index, a key gauge of service-sector inflation, up 3.7% on a year earlier in September. Reuters says the figure points to mounting price pressures.

squawks.headline: China industrial profits rise 14.4% y/y in September, up from 4.2% in August; year-to-date growth eases to 15.5%
squawks.detail: China's statistics bureau says industrial profits for January to September are up 15.5% on a year earlier, compared with 15.7% for the year to August. September profits alone rose 14.4% year on year.

squawks.headline: People's Bank of China injects 1 trillion yuan through overnight reverse repos
squawks.detail: China's central bank said in a statement that it had added 1 trillion yuan of liquidity through overnight reverse repurchase operations.

squawks.headline: Russia-Ukraine ceasefire in Oleshky takes effect; Russia suspends strikes on Kherson
squawks.detail: The local ceasefire in Oleshky came into force, according to reports. Russia's Defence Ministry said it has suspended strikes on Ukraine's Kherson.

squawks.headline: UK BRC shop price inflation rises to 2.1% in the year to October from 1.4% in September
squawks.detail: The British Retail Consortium's figures put annual shop price inflation at 2.1% in October, up from 1.4% in September. Retailers told the Chancellor that discounting is no longer holding back price rises, City AM reports.

squawks.headline: USTR Greer warns EIB loan to Airbus may breach the US-EU trade truce and aircraft agreement
squawks.detail: US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said the European Investment Bank's loan to Airbus may violate the US-EU trade truce. He said US concerns need to be resolved quickly to avoid breaching the large civil aircraft agreement, the FT also reports.

squawks.headline: South Korea Q3 GDP grows 1.0% q/q and 3.4% y/y, beating poll forecasts
squawks.detail: The Bank of Korea's advance estimate shows Q3 GDP up 1.0% on the quarter against a 0.7% poll, and up 3.4% on the year against 3.0%. Private consumption fell 0.2% q/q. A BoK official said the Q3 figure adds 0.35 percentage points to this year's growth forecast.

squawks.headline: Healey's Budget to centre on everyday cost-of-living fixes with limited giveaways and first-time buyer help, FT reports
squawks.detail: The Financial Times reports that Chancellor Healey is set to offer limited measures to ease living costs as energy costs rise, along with support for first-time homeowners, in Wednesday's Budget.

squawks.headline: Canadian PM Carney says any progress in US trade talks reflects the US moving towards Canada's position
squawks.detail: Canada's Prime Minister Carney commented on the state of trade negotiations with the US, saying any progress made has come from the US shifting closer to Canada's stance.

squawks.headline: Canadian PM Carney says Canada will not sign the trade terms the US offered in August
squawks.detail: Canada's prime minister said Ottawa is not prepared to accept the US trade terms put forward in August. This follows reports that the two countries are working on a deal to ease US tariffs on Canadian steel and car imports.

squawks.headline: UK reportedly in talks with the EU on a return to free movement, The Times reports
squawks.detail: The Times reports that the UK is holding talks with the EU on a return to free movement. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Iran is open to a shorter timeline on the US proposal if conditions are met, state TV reports
squawks.detail: Iranian state television reported that Tehran is willing to accept a shorter timeline for the US proposal, provided certain conditions are met. The report did not say what the conditions were.

squawks.headline: US and Canada reportedly work on deal to ease US tariffs on Canadian steel and car imports
squawks.detail: Unnamed sources say the US and Canada are working on an agreement that would ease US tariffs on imports of Canadian steel and cars. The reports give no timing or terms.

squawks.headline: Poll: 13 of 23 economists see RBNZ cash rate at 3.00% by year-end, while 9 expect a rise to 3.25% in December
squawks.detail: In a poll of economists, 13 of 23 expect the Reserve Bank of New Zealand's cash rate to end the year at 3.00%. Nine expect a further increase to 3.25% in December.

squawks.headline: Poll finds 22 of 27 economists expect RBNZ to raise cash rate 25bp to 3.00% on 28 October
squawks.detail: In a poll of economists, 22 of 27 said they expect the Reserve Bank of New Zealand to raise its cash rate by 25bp to 3.00% at its 28 October decision.

squawks.headline: New York Fed's Williams forecasts no Fed rate rises in 2027, against market expectations
squawks.detail: New York Fed President John Williams projects no rate increases in 2027, according to a market news report that says his view differs from market pricing. It comes ahead of this week's Fed policy meeting.

squawks.headline: US official warns Iran it must change its behaviour or face completion of the mission, Al Jazeera reports
squawks.detail: Al Jazeera cites an unnamed US official issuing the warning to Tehran. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Reform UK leader Farage says banks should not face new taxes in this week's Budget, partly reversing his earlier stance
squawks.detail: City AM reports that Farage has come out against new bank taxes in Wednesday's Budget. Earlier this year he had pledged to scrap the interest lenders receive on their deposits at the Bank of England.

squawks.headline: EU Council adopts eight European Peace Facility decisions for Ukraine, taking total EPF support to €10.8bn
squawks.detail: The EU Council says €4.7bn will reimburse member states for military aid to Ukraine and €230m will go to the EU military assistance mission for Ukraine (EUMAM). The decisions take the EU's overall European Peace Facility support for Ukraine to €10.8bn.

squawks.headline: Canada says partners will sign founding articles of new Defence, Security and Resilience Bank in Luxembourg on 30 November
squawks.detail: Canadian Finance Minister Francois-Philippe Champagne said in a statement on Monday that Canada and its partners will meet in Luxembourg on 30 November to sign the articles of agreement that establish the bank.

squawks.headline: Government expected to publish a fiscal devolution roadmap for England alongside Wednesday's Budget
squawks.detail: Centre for Cities says the government is expected to publish a roadmap for fiscal devolution in England on Wednesday alongside the Budget.

squawks.headline: UK National Living Wage for over-21s reportedly set to rise 3.9% from £12.71 to about £13.20
squawks.detail: A report carried by a market news feed says the National Living Wage, which covers workers aged 21 and over, is expected to go up from £12.71 to around £13.20, a 3.9% increase. It adds figures to earlier reports that the minimum wage will rise in Wednesday's Budget.

squawks.headline: Saudi Arabia reportedly offers Houthis $1bn in Iran-brokered deal to end attacks, Israel Hayom reports
squawks.detail: Israeli newspaper Israel Hayom reports that Saudi Arabia has offered the Houthis $1bn under a deal brokered by Iran to stop their attacks. The report has not been confirmed.

squawks.headline: Healey to raise minimum wage by nearly 4% in Budget but slow increase for young workers, The Times reports
squawks.detail: The Times reports that Chancellor Healey will announce an increase of nearly 4% in the minimum wage, with a slower rise for younger workers. The Budget is due on Wednesday.

squawks.headline: US $69bn 2-year note auction clears at 4.708%, tailing by 0.3bp; bid-to-cover slips to 2.59
squawks.detail: The US Treasury sold $69bn of 2-year notes at a high yield of 4.708%, against 4.705% when-issued before the sale and 4.787% at the previous auction. Bid-to-cover was 2.59 against 2.63 previously; primary dealers took 13%, directs 41.32% and indirects 45.68%.

squawks.headline: US 2-year when-issued yield stands at 4.705% ahead of $69bn Treasury auction
squawks.detail: The when-issued US 2-year note yield was 4.705% shortly before the US Treasury's $69bn 2-year note auction.

squawks.headline: EU foreign policy chief Kallas says further Russia sanctions are being prepared and warns of a serious risk of renewed Iran-US escalation
squawks.detail: EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said more sanctions on Russia are being prepared. She also said there is a serious risk of renewed escalation between Iran and the US.

squawks.headline: Federal Reserve bids for US 2-year notes total $7.7bn
squawks.detail: Federal Reserve bids for US 2-year Treasury notes come to $7.7bn, a market commentator account reports.

squawks.headline: Trump administration challenges US wind projects, putting a bipartisan energy permitting deal in doubt, FT reports
squawks.detail: The Financial Times reports that the administration's new challenge to wind power projects ends a truce on renewables. That truce was aimed at winning bipartisan support for a permitting bill.

squawks.headline: Brent crude recovers its earlier losses and trades close to $117 a barrel
squawks.detail: A market newswire reports that Brent has turned around its earlier fall and is trading near $117 a barrel. Crude had fallen earlier in the day while Qatar was pursuing mediation efforts.

squawks.headline: Iran, Turkey, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia agree to keep talking after Tehran meeting, Iranian state media reports
squawks.detail: Iranian state broadcaster IRIB reports that Iran, Turkey, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia have agreed to continue talks. The four met in Tehran on Monday in talks aimed at ending the conflict.

squawks.headline: US 3-month bill auction clears at 4.05% and 6-month at 4.21%; 6-month cover falls to 2.63
squawks.detail: The US Treasury sold $95bn of 3-month bills at a high yield of 4.050% with bid-to-cover of 3.07, up from 2.770, and 82.29% of bids at the high were allotted. It also sold $82bn of 6-month bills at 4.210%, against 4.220% previously, with cover of 2.63, down from 2.840, and 61.74% of bids at the high allotted.

squawks.headline: Iran is at an advanced stage of planning attacks on Americans, Fox News reports
squawks.detail: Fox News reported on Monday that Iran is at an advanced stage of planning attacks on Americans. The batch reports no market reaction and no official confirmation.

squawks.headline: US Strategic Petroleum Reserve crude stocks drop to 282.6 million barrels, the lowest level since 1982
squawks.detail: Crude held in the US Strategic Petroleum Reserve fell to 282.6 million barrels last week, the lowest level since 1982, according to a market news feed.

squawks.headline: US Treasury plans to buy back up to $6bn of longer-dated debt on Tuesday
squawks.detail: The US Treasury will hold a buyback operation on Tuesday for up to $6bn of longer-dated securities.

squawks.headline: Iran's president repeats that Tehran is not seeking nuclear weapons
squawks.detail: Iran's president said again on Monday that Tehran is not trying to acquire nuclear weapons. The statement came during the Mecca pact talks being held in Tehran.

squawks.headline: Slovak foreign minister says Russia told him it stands ready to honour agreed energy contracts
squawks.detail: Slovakia's foreign minister made the remarks after meeting Russian Foreign Minister Lavrov. He added that Slovakia will keep working with Russia in areas that sanctions do not cover.

squawks.headline: US Dallas Fed manufacturing index rises to 13.4 in October, above the 8.8 forecast
squawks.detail: The Dallas Fed manufacturing business index came in at 13.4 for October, against a forecast of 8.8 and a previous reading of 9.8.

squawks.headline: UK 20-year gilt yield falls 6bp to 5.678%, its lowest since 23 September
squawks.detail: The 20-year gilt yield was down 6bp on the day at 5.678%, its lowest level since 23 September, a market feed reported at 14:21 UTC.

squawks.headline: Iran's President Pezeshkian tells Saudi, Pakistani and Turkish delegations that Tehran is ready to deepen cooperation and settle differences
squawks.detail: The Iranian presidency reported the remarks from Pezeshkian's meeting with the three delegations in Tehran. Iranian state broadcaster IRIB separately reported that Iran is ready to back any understanding on regional unity.

squawks.headline: German Chancellor Merz meets Knot and Hernández de Cos, seen as favourites for top ECB post, Handelsblatt reports
squawks.detail: Handelsblatt reports that Merz held meetings with the two candidates, who are described as front-runners for the top job at the ECB.

squawks.headline: Senior Iranian official says Tehran talks with Mecca pact members exclude Iran's nuclear programme
squawks.detail: A senior Iranian official said the talks with Mecca pact members in Tehran do not include the nuclear issue. The official added that Iran will not discuss its nuclear programme until Tehran's demands are met.

squawks.headline: Egypt's parliament authorises the military to help defend Saudi Arabia if the kingdom asks for support
squawks.detail: Egyptian MPs voted to approve military support for Saudi Arabia's defence, to be given on a Saudi request. The vote follows Houthi missile and drone attacks aimed at Saudi Arabia. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: French 10-year yield extends its fall, down as much as 10.56bp on the day to 4.9158%
squawks.detail: The French 10-year yield fell as much as 10.56bp on the day to 4.9158%, a bigger drop than the 5.3bp decline reported earlier after Moody's left France's sovereign rating unchanged.

squawks.headline: US Chicago Fed National Activity Index rises to 0.07 for September, above the -0.095 forecast
squawks.detail: The Chicago Fed National Activity Index for September came in at 0.07, against a forecast of -0.095 and a previous reading of -0.04.

squawks.headline: US natural gas futures drop 5% to lowest since April 2026 on higher output and weaker demand forecasts
squawks.detail: US natural gas futures extended losses to fall 5%, reaching their lowest level since April 2026. The decline was attributed to higher output and forecasts of lower demand.

squawks.headline: Banks face an expected tax raid in Wednesday's Budget; London mayor Khan urges them to keep investing in the UK
squawks.detail: City AM reports that the banking sector is expected to face higher taxes in Chancellor Healey's Budget. On Monday, London mayor Sadiq Khan urged the biggest banks to stay in London but would not say whether he opposed the measure.

squawks.headline: Healey's Budget to exempt nearly one million state-pension-dependent retirees from income tax, City AM reports
squawks.detail: City AM reports that Chancellor Healey's Autumn Budget this week will exempt low-income pensioners who rely on the state pension from income tax. A former pensions minister has warned that the plan could create a £200m cliff edge and a growing bill for future governments.

squawks.headline: Saudi Arabia backs opening negotiation channels as Mecca pact talks take place in Tehran, aiming to end the conflict
squawks.detail: Saudi Arabia said the negotiations were meant to prevent escalation and open the way to an agreement ending the conflict. It made the comments against the background of Mecca pact talks in Tehran.

squawks.headline: Egypt's foreign minister says a military solution with Iran cannot last and Cairo is working to prevent a full-scale war
squawks.detail: Egypt's foreign minister said Cairo talks every day with both Iran and the US, and that it is trying to avoid another full military conflict. He added that a military solution would not be sustainable.

squawks.headline: Large gilt investors want reassurance from Healey's Budget and caution against changes to the fiscal rules, FT reports
squawks.detail: The Financial Times reports that big bond investors want the new Chancellor's Budget on Wednesday to reassure the gilt market. They warn against adjusting the key fiscal rules.

squawks.headline: UK CBI distributive trades balance improves to -10, well above the -48 forecast and the previous -55
squawks.detail: The CBI distributive trades survey's reported sales balance came in at -10, against a forecast of -48 and a previous reading of -55.

squawks.headline: Fed policymakers have signalled no rate rise this week, but investors expect the pause to be short, Reuters reports
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that Federal Reserve officials have indicated they will leave US short-term rates unchanged at this week's meeting. It also reports that, with inflation still the main concern, investors do not expect the pause to last long.

squawks.headline: Ministers plan apprenticeship funding overhaul that would make training over-25s more expensive, Guardian reports
squawks.detail: The Guardian reports that ministers are planning to change apprenticeship funding so that training workers over 25 costs more. Employers warn the change could undermine the government's plan to tackle youth unemployment.

squawks.headline: Pakistan's central bank lifts its key rate to 12%, citing inflation risks from the Gulf conflict
squawks.detail: Pakistan's central bank raised its key policy rate to 12%. It pointed to inflation risks from the conflict in the Gulf.

squawks.headline: ECB survey finds euro zone firms are struggling more to get bank credit as fuel and other costs rise
squawks.detail: A European Central Bank survey published on Monday showed firms in the euro zone finding it harder to obtain credit from banks, while higher fuel and other costs squeeze their finances, Reuters reports.

squawks.headline: Kremlin says Oleshky truce could be a model for other local ceasefires; renewed talks with Ukraine and US do not limit fighting
squawks.detail: The Kremlin said the local ceasefire in Oleshky, agreed with US help, could set a precedent for similar ceasefires elsewhere. It added that the agreement to resume three-way talks with Ukraine and the US places no restrictions on either Moscow or Kyiv continuing military action.

squawks.headline: Kalshi traders price a 93% chance the Fed holds this week and a 6% chance of a hike; Goldman expects a December rise
squawks.detail: Kalshi prediction-market pricing shows a 93% chance the Fed holds this week and 6% for a hike. Goldman Sachs expects a hold now and a 25bp rise in December.

squawks.headline: Chancellor Healey reportedly plans to borrow billions for military investment in Wednesday's Budget
squawks.detail: City AM cites reports that the Chancellor will fund defence investment with borrowing in the Budget. UK defence shares rose in early Monday trading, with Rolls-Royce up nearly 2% and Melrose up 1.4%.

squawks.headline: Healey pledges more than £1bn extra for social and affordable housing as figures show a sharp fall in housebuilding
squawks.detail: City AM reports that the extra funding will be confirmed in Wednesday's Budget and will extend the government's 10-year social and affordable housing programme. New figures show a sharp fall in housebuilding, raising doubts over the 1.5m homes target.

squawks.headline: German Ifo expectations rise to 91.6, beating forecast, while current conditions slip to 88.8, below forecast
squawks.detail: The October Ifo expectations index came in at 91.6, against a 90 forecast and 90.4 previously. The current conditions index was 88.8, against an 89.8 forecast and 89.5 previously.

squawks.headline: German Ifo business climate index comes in at 90.2, above the 89.9 forecast and the previous reading
squawks.detail: The Ifo institute's German business climate index came in at 90.2 against a forecast of 89.9. The previous reading was also 89.9.

squawks.headline: Chancellor Healey expected to deliver a cautious first Budget this week, putting gilt market stability first, Reuters reports
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that Chancellor John Healey is expected to favour bond market stability over large spending increases in this week's Budget. The report contrasts this with the bigger spending plans PM Burnham discussed when he took office.

squawks.headline: EU plans import curbs on Chinese chemicals and furniture, which could be presented as early as Q1 2027
squawks.detail: Reports say the EU is planning import restrictions on Chinese chemicals and furniture and is also looking at caps or quotas on Chinese furniture. The new trade measures could be presented as early as the first quarter of 2027.

squawks.headline: Singapore agrees with Saudi Aramco to store Saudi oil in rock caverns, FT reports
squawks.detail: The Financial Times reports that the deal with Saudi Aramco is meant to secure energy supplies for south-east Asia while the Middle East war disrupts supply.

squawks.headline: Iran says Monday's talks will take in Israel, Lebanon and Palestine; warns of a crushing response to any aggressors
squawks.detail: Iran said the talks on Monday will cover Israel, Lebanon and Palestine. Separately, it said its forces would respond with crushing force to aggressors.

squawks.headline: French 10-year yield falls 5.3bp to 4.9685% after Moody's keeps France's sovereign rating unchanged
squawks.detail: France's 10-year government bond yield falls 5.3bp to 4.9685% in early trading. The move follows Moody's decision on Friday to leave France's sovereign rating unchanged.

squawks.headline: Markets price only 12% odds of a Fed rate rise at this week's meeting
squawks.detail: An economist reports that markets see a 12% chance of a Fed hike at this week's meeting. He contrasts this with July, when markets pushed for a rise from Chair Warsh.

squawks.headline: PM Burnham says Healey will set out on Wednesday how the UK meets NATO commitments; signals savings from youth job support
squawks.detail: Prime Minister Burnham said Chancellor Healey would set out the path to meeting the UK's NATO commitments on Wednesday, and that youth job support needs changing in a way that can save money. Speaking on the same occasion, he also said he would like to see the UK rejoin the EU in his lifetime.

squawks.headline: PM Burnham says he is not proposing that the UK rejoin the EU in this parliament and rules out an early election
squawks.detail: Prime Minister Andy Burnham made the remarks in an ITV interview on 26 October. He said he was not proposing EU membership during the current parliament and ruled out calling an early general election.

squawks.headline: Swedish producer prices rise 3.4% on the month, taking the annual rate to 11.2% from 6.8%
squawks.detail: Swedish PPI rose 3.4% month on month, up from 0.9% previously, and annual producer price inflation reached 11.2% against 6.8% before. No forecast was given.

squawks.headline: Fed to keep raising rates quarterly after reversing its 2025 insurance cuts, FT reports
squawks.detail: The Financial Times reports that the Federal Reserve plans to keep its rate increases on a quarterly pace now that the insurance cuts made in 2025 have been reversed.

squawks.headline: Crude oil falls as Qatar pursues mediation efforts, FT reports
squawks.detail: The Financial Times reports that crude oil prices are falling as Qatar pursues mediation. No price levels were given.

squawks.headline: EU leaders aim to finalise €45bn Ukraine loan backed by the EU budget before year-end
squawks.detail: EU leaders are seeking to complete a €45 billion loan to Ukraine, guaranteed by the EU budget, before the end of the year.

squawks.headline: Houthis claim drone attack on Saudi Arabia's East-West crude pumping stations and Riyadh airport; Saudi Arabia has not confirmed
squawks.detail: Yemen's Houthi group said on Monday it had targeted Saudi Arabia's East-West crude oil pumping stations and King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, with no immediate Saudi confirmation. Reuters reported that oil prices slipped on Monday from near six-month highs, while the attacks on Saudi Arabia kept supply concerns in focus.

squawks.headline: Saudi-led coalition destroys Houthi missile launchers in Sanaa after intercepting ballistic missile fired at Riyadh
squawks.detail: The Saudi-led coalition said its air defences intercepted a Houthi ballistic missile aimed at Riyadh. It then destroyed two launch platforms in Sanaa, one of them used in that attack, and said its operation against the Houthi ballistic missile network is continuing.

squawks.headline: China's onshore yuan strengthens to 6.6682 per dollar, strongest since June 2022, after PBOC sets firmest fixing since 2023
squawks.detail: The PBOC set the yuan midpoint at 6.7162 per dollar, against 6.7180 previously, its strongest fixing since 2 February 2023. The onshore yuan then rose to 6.6682 in early trade, its strongest level since 9 June 2022.

squawks.headline: RBA signals interest rates could go higher; Australian dollar weakens
squawks.detail: The Reserve Bank of Australia signalled that higher interest rates are possible. The Australian dollar still weakened, according to reports early on Monday in Asia.

squawks.headline: White House adviser Hassett says US-Canada trade deal is very close; Trump says tariff dispute will be settled soon
squawks.detail: Hassett said Commerce Secretary Lutnick is still negotiating, although US officials cautioned that progress was uncertain because Canada had not offered enough concessions. Speaking at a Michigan border rally, Trump said the dispute would be resolved soon but did not say what a deal would involve.

squawks.headline: UK government commits a further £432mn to end rough sleeping ahead of the Budget
squawks.detail: The government has committed a further £432mn to ending rough sleeping. The FT reports that PM Burnham is promising Budget money for the goal, while Chancellor Healey is preparing a fiscal statement intended to reassure markets.

squawks.headline: European gas prices hit their highest level since 2022 as trading opens
squawks.detail: European gas prices reached their highest level since 2022 at the start of trading, according to a market report. No percentage move was given.

squawks.headline: Chancellor Healey expected to announce a 3.9% rise in the full state pension, The Times reports
squawks.detail: The Times reports that Chancellor John Healey is expected to announce a 3.9% increase to the full state pension.

squawks.headline: UK will not join the Canada-led Defence Security and Resilience Bank and will back a separate UK-led initiative
squawks.detail: The FT and Reuters, citing a source familiar with the matter, report that Britain will stay out of the Canada-led defence bank. Reuters adds that the UK and Canada said they would build a framework for cooperation between their defence-funding initiatives.

squawks.headline: Canadian dollar reaches five-week high against US dollar as bets on a Bank of Canada rate rise next week build
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that the Canadian dollar firmed to a five-week high against the US dollar on Friday. It says higher oil prices and domestic retail sales data supported expectations that the Bank of Canada will raise rates next week.

squawks.headline: French finance minister Lescure says Moody's decision acknowledges the strength of the French economy
squawks.detail: France's finance minister Lescure responded on Friday evening to Moody's ratings review of France. The post did not say what Moody's decided.

squawks.headline: Moody's says the recent sharp rise in French government bond yields adds to the risk of debt affordability weakening further
squawks.detail: The ratings agency made the point in its review of France, after a week of heavy selling in French government bonds. No yield figures were given.

squawks.headline: Moody's France review says slower growth and higher deficit have increased debt burden; projects 2027 deficit at 5.2% of GDP
squawks.detail: In its periodic review of France, Moody's says slower growth and a higher deficit have pushed the debt burden up since its last review, and it projects a deficit of 5.2% of GDP in 2027. The agency says France's Aa3 rating assumes that a deficit-reducing budget for 2027 is adopted.

squawks.headline: US Treasuries and stocks fall together as higher oil prices revive inflation concerns
squawks.detail: A US market wrap posted at the close reports that both US bonds and equities fell, with the surge in oil prices renewing inflation worries. No yield levels were given.

squawks.headline: Trump says the US is close to ending the Russia-Ukraine war, though he adds that it is only a hope
squawks.detail: US President Trump said he hopes the end of the Russia-Ukraine war is close. He spoke after the White House announced a local ceasefire in Oleshky. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: White House changes the list of Canadian goods under Section 338 tariffs from 30 October, swapping plywood and paper for valves and carpets
squawks.detail: The White House said plywood sheets, some paper products, certain machinery, refrigeration equipment and packing crates and boxes are being taken out of the Section 338 tariffs. It said they will be replaced by certain valves, carpets, waste products and other goods, with both changes taking effect on 30 October 2026.

squawks.headline: Trump says the US may carry out another operation against Iran and doubts Tehran is ready to negotiate seriously
squawks.detail: US President Trump made the remarks at a rally in Fort Myers, Florida, on 23 October. He said he does not expect Iran to agree to get down to business.

squawks.headline: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say two tankers hit naval mines on an unauthorised route south of the Strait of Hormuz
squawks.detail: Iranian state media carried the Revolutionary Guards' statement that two tankers struck naval mines while using an unauthorised route south of the Strait of Hormuz. The inputs report no market reaction.

squawks.headline: Iran says the blockade of its southern ports has cut its imports by 25%, ISNA reports
squawks.detail: Iran's Students News Agency (ISNA) reports that Iran puts the fall in its imports caused by the blockade of its southern ports at 25%. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Iraq's prime minister sets a goal of gradually lifting oil output to 10 mln bpd by 2032
squawks.detail: Iraq's prime minister said the country plans to raise oil production step by step to 10 million barrels per day by 2032. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Brent crude futures settle at $116.72 a barrel, up $3.55 or 3.14% on the day
squawks.detail: A market commentator reports that Brent crude futures settled $3.55, or 3.14%, higher at $116.72 a barrel. WTI also settled higher earlier in the session.

squawks.headline: WTI crude futures settle at $103.27 a barrel, up $3.80 or 3.82% on the day
squawks.detail: US crude oil futures settled at $103.27 a barrel on Friday, a gain of $3.80 or 3.82%. Earlier in the session the gains had been linked to worries over escalation in the Middle East.

squawks.headline: Downing Street says Burnham backed Saudi Arabia over Houthi attacks and raised Argentina's Falklands measures in call with Trump
squawks.detail: Downing Street's readout of the Burnham–Trump call says the prime minister restated UK support for Saudi Arabia in the face of Houthi attacks. It also says he raised the economic consequences for the UK and US of Argentina's coercive measures over the Falkland Islands, and that the two leaders agreed approving the Jackdaw field will benefit the UK.

squawks.headline: Downing Street says PM Burnham and Trump discussed the energy secretary's approval of the Jackdaw gas field
squawks.detail: Downing Street's readout of the call between the UK prime minister and the US president says the two discussed the energy secretary's decision to approve the Jackdaw North Sea development. It also says Burnham stressed that Ukraine needs full access to Starlink.

squawks.headline: Trump removes US tariffs on nine categories of Canadian goods, Senator Collins' office says
squawks.detail: US Senator Collins' office says nine product categories from Canada will be exempted from US tariffs, including blueberries, potatoes, apples and seaweed. Collins says Trump has removed the tariffs on these goods.

squawks.headline: China's energy regulator tells oil and gas firms to raise output capacity and speed up national strategic supply bases
squawks.detail: China's National Energy Administration has told the country's oil and gas companies to expand production capacity and to speed up building national strategic oil and gas supply bases, Reuters reports. It also said the firms should take responsibility for safeguarding national energy security.

squawks.headline: US could offset any cut in tariffs on Canada by raising other levies, WSJ reports
squawks.detail: The Wall Street Journal reports that the US may balance tariff reductions for Canada with increases in other levies. This follows its earlier report that President Trump is expected to lift some US tariffs on Canada.

squawks.headline: Trump is expected to lift some US tariffs on Canada, WSJ reports
squawks.detail: The Wall Street Journal reports that President Trump is expected to remove some tariffs on Canada. The report links the move to an effort to help Senator Susan Collins.

squawks.headline: Trump has told CENTCOM to draw up a plan for striking Iran, with no deadline set, Israel's Kan reports
squawks.detail: Israeli public broadcaster Kan reports that the US president directed Central Command to prepare a strike plan against Iran, and that no deadline was attached. The report comes after Trump said the US would not attack Iran before the midterm elections.

squawks.headline: Ukraine and Russia sign agreement setting out details of Oleshky humanitarian mission, Kyiv ombudsman says
squawks.detail: Ukraine's ombudsman Lubinets says the multi-stage mission will cover demining roads to Oleshky, food deliveries and evacuations. He says Kyiv is working to extend the mission to other settlements.

squawks.headline: Iran has drawn up detailed plans to strike Gulf undersea cables if the war resumes, officials say
squawks.detail: A market news account reported the claim, citing unnamed officials. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: German oil stockpiling agency EBV launches tender to sell diesel, heating oil and crude from its reserves
squawks.detail: Germany's oil stockpiling agency EBV issued a tender on Friday to sell diesel, heating oil and crude oil from its reserves. The post gave no volumes.

squawks.headline: Poll finds most economists expect the Bank of Canada to raise its overnight rate to 2.50% on 28 October
squawks.detail: A poll found 19 of 34 economists expect a rise to 2.50% on 28 October, and 16 of 29 expect two rises by the end of March. In the August poll, 17 of 34 had forecast no change until mid-2027.

squawks.headline: Russian military says Oleshky ceasefire begins at 04:00 local time on 27 October for a humanitarian operation
squawks.detail: Russia's defence ministry says the ceasefire in Russian-controlled Oleshky in the Kherson direction starts at 04:00 local time on 27 October, Interfax reports. Chief of the general staff Gerasimov says Russian forces will make sure a humanitarian convoy can move safely to Alekseyevka with essential goods.

squawks.headline: October marks the worst month on record for attacks on commercial shipping in and around the Strait of Hormuz
squawks.detail: Reuters reports the figure from data compiled by a Washington-based think tank that has tracked maritime security incidents worldwide since 2017.

squawks.headline: Trump says the US will not attack Iran before the midterm elections and that talks are under way
squawks.detail: US President Trump said the US would not strike Iran before the midterms and that talks with Tehran are in progress. The posts do not report any market reaction.

squawks.headline: Zelenskiy says any peace deal would need strong security guarantees and 10 years of funding for Ukraine's army
squawks.detail: Ukraine's president set out the conditions for any peace agreement with Russia: strong security guarantees and funding for 10 years to maintain the Ukrainian army. The comments come as the Kremlin says three-way talks with the US are planned for early November.

squawks.headline: Kremlin says Russian and Ukrainian militaries are still setting the dates for the Oleshky ceasefire
squawks.detail: The Kremlin said civilians who want to leave Oleshky will be allowed to go. It praised Melania Trump for coordinating the humanitarian agreement and said Putin and Trump had discussed it in a recent phone call.

squawks.headline: Trump says the US is very close to a trade deal with Mexico and that Canada is working hard on one
squawks.detail: US President Trump said a deal with Mexico was close. In the same remarks he said Canada was working hard to reach a deal with the US.

squawks.headline: Trump says he discussed opening up North Sea oil in a call with the UK prime minister
squawks.detail: US President Trump said he talked about opening up North Sea oil with UK prime minister Burnham today. Some earlier posts described the call as being with the British foreign minister.

squawks.headline: Trump says the US could end the Iran war quickly and claims control of the Strait of Hormuz and its oil
squawks.detail: US President Trump said the US could bring the Iran war to a rapid end and that the question is whether to finish it or let it wither. He also said the Strait of Hormuz belongs to the US, that the US is taking out as much oil as it wants and that it could take all of Iran's oil.

squawks.headline: Turkish foreign minister says no one backs a fresh attack on Iran and that diplomacy is the only route
squawks.detail: Turkey's foreign minister spoke after talks with regional and European counterparts. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: German foreign minister says Russia is being urged to agree a new Black Sea security deal
squawks.detail: Germany's foreign minister said he and his counterparts are jointly urging Russia to agree a new security arrangement for the Black Sea. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Senior Ukrainian official says Oleshky ceasefire will take effect soon, with humanitarian corridors to follow in coming days
squawks.detail: A senior Ukrainian official said the ceasefire in Russian-occupied Oleshky will be established soon and that humanitarian corridors out of the town will be set up in the coming days.

squawks.headline: German foreign minister says Germany, France and the UK are ready to negotiate with Iran, stressing urgency to avoid escalation
squawks.detail: Germany's foreign minister said there is great urgency to avoid a new escalation, and that Germany, France and the UK stand ready to negotiate with Iran. He also called for support for Saudi Arabia and the Yemeni government in their defence, and said there was agreement to do everything possible to allow Russian and Ukrainian grain exports.

squawks.headline: EU trade chief Sefcovic says the EU's trade deficit with China could exceed the 2022 record
squawks.detail: EU Trade Commissioner Maros Sefcovic said the bloc's trade deficit with China could surpass its 2022 record. He spoke as EU ministers seek deals with Beijing to limit Chinese imports.

squawks.headline: Zelenskiy says Russia has started its winter attacks and US Patriot interceptor deliveries are still delayed
squawks.detail: Ukraine's President Zelenskiy said Russia has already begun its winter campaign of attacks. He said delivery of missile interceptors is still delayed and that he hopes the US will deliver Patriot interceptors.

squawks.headline: Zelenskiy says Ukraine has agreed to a team-level trilateral meeting after a call with US envoys Witkoff and Kushner
squawks.detail: Ukraine's president said he had spoken with US envoys Witkoff and Kushner, and that a trilateral meeting at team level had been agreed. Russia had already agreed to resume trilateral talks with the US and Ukraine.

squawks.headline: US University of Michigan final October 5-year inflation expectations hold at 3.5%, in line with forecast
squawks.detail: The final October University of Michigan survey puts 5-year inflation expectations at 3.5%. That matches both the forecast and the previous reading.

squawks.headline: US University of Michigan final October consumer sentiment comes in at 48, above the 46.3 forecast
squawks.detail: The final October reading of University of Michigan consumer sentiment was 48, against a forecast of 46.3. The expectations index was 48.8, above the 47.1 forecast and up from 47.3 previously.

squawks.headline: US Energy Department authorises emergency exchange of up to 400,000 barrels of crude from the SPR
squawks.detail: The US Department of Energy authorised an emergency exchange of up to 400,000 barrels of crude oil from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve. It is to address a crude supply disruption affecting the Phillips 66 Lake Charles refinery in Louisiana.

squawks.headline: French foreign minister Barrot warns renewed Iran-US escalation would hurt everyone and push oil prices higher
squawks.detail: France's foreign minister Jean-Noël Barrot said any new escalation between Iran and the United States would leave no winners and would raise oil prices. The remarks follow US strikes on Iran and threats of retaliation from Tehran.

squawks.headline: US flash services PMI slips to 57.9 in October from 58.8, near the 58 forecast; manufacturing edges up to 56
squawks.detail: S&P Global's US flash services PMI came in at 57.9 against a forecast of 58 and a previous 58.8. The flash manufacturing PMI rose to 56, above the 55.5 forecast and up from 55.9.

squawks.headline: White House says Russia and Ukraine agree a local ceasefire in Oleshky, starting 29 October, brokered by Melania Trump
squawks.detail: The White House says Russia and Ukraine will temporarily halt all military action in the city of Oleshky so humanitarian aid can enter and a civilian evacuation can be prepared through a safe corridor. It credits Melania Trump with securing the deal and says the ceasefire begins on 29 October.

squawks.headline: USTR proposes extending suspension of its Section 301 probe into China's maritime and shipbuilding sectors to 9 January 2027
squawks.detail: The Office of the US Trade Representative proposed a further suspension of its Section 301 investigation into China's targeting of the maritime, logistics and shipbuilding sectors, running to 9 January 2027.

squawks.headline: Algeria tells urea fertiliser producers to halt supplies to France as France raises Algerian trade curbs at EU level, sources say
squawks.detail: Sources say Algeria has instructed urea producers to stop supplying France, following an informal ban on imports of French products in place since July. France has taken the issue of Algerian trade restrictions to EU level, according to the same sources.

squawks.headline: Canadian retail sales rise 1.2% on the month in August, just under the 1.3% forecast; core sales also up 1.2%
squawks.detail: Headline retail sales rose 1.2% month on month in August against a 1.3% forecast, after -0.7% previously. Core retail sales also rose 1.2%, ahead of the 1.1% forecast, after -0.7% previously.

squawks.headline: WTI crude extends gains, rising more than $2 to $101.62 a barrel on worries over Middle East escalation
squawks.detail: US WTI futures climbed by more than $2 a barrel to $101.62, adding to gains as concern grew over rising tension in the Middle East. In the previous session WTI settled at $99.47 and Brent at $113.17.

squawks.headline: Sterling rises to a fresh 17-month high against the euro after mixed UK data
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that sterling edged up to its highest level against the euro in 17 months on Friday. It is on course for a fourth straight weekly gain after UK data sent mixed signals on the economy.

squawks.headline: EU ministers seek deals with Beijing to limit Chinese imports in chemicals, machinery and pharmaceuticals
squawks.detail: EU ministers said on Friday that the bloc should pursue agreements with China to curb imports in several sectors, calling the goods trade deficit with China unsustainable and damaging, Reuters reports.

squawks.headline: Reuters dealer poll sees 2026/27 gilt sales raised by £3.4bn to £249.6bn, with long-dated share lowest since 1990
squawks.detail: Bond dealers polled by Reuters ahead of the Budget also see 2026/27 T-bill sales up £5bn to £10bn, public sector net borrowing up about £15bn in both 2026/27 and 2027/28, and headroom of £15bn.

squawks.headline: France awaits a Moody's ratings verdict today after a week of heavy selling in French government bonds spread to Italy
squawks.detail: Reuters reports France faces the risk of a Moody's downgrade on Friday while its government struggles with social unrest and strained public finances. Economist Robin Brooks says French government debt sold off sharply this week and the selling spread to Italy, while yields fell in most other markets, especially the US and Japan.

squawks.headline: Bank of Russia holds its key rate at 14%, as forecast
squawks.detail: The Russian central bank left its key interest rate unchanged at 14%, in line with the 14% forecast and the previous level.

squawks.headline: Markets stop pricing a Fed rate hike in December as AI sell-off shifts rate expectations, Reuters reports
squawks.detail: Reuters says markets no longer expect the Federal Reserve to raise rates in December. It links the change in rate expectations to the sell-off in AI-related stocks.

squawks.headline: Germany says an electricity tax cut is on the agenda but depends on budget financing; revenue cost put at about €5bn a year
squawks.detail: A German government spokesperson said a cut to electricity tax is under consideration, subject to sufficient budget financing being found. A ministry spokesperson said it would reduce annual tax revenues by about €5bn.

squawks.headline: Kremlin says three-way Ukraine talks with the US are set for Abu Dhabi in early November
squawks.detail: The Kremlin said the talks on Ukraine will take place in Abu Dhabi in early November in a three-party format, Interfax reported. An earlier report had pointed to technical talks possibly in mid-November.

squawks.headline: Trump administration ends programme that rewarded allies for aligning with US export controls
squawks.detail: A market news account reports that the US administration has halted a programme that rewarded allied countries for aligning with US export controls. No further details or market reaction were reported.

squawks.headline: UK October flash PMI shows employment rising for the first time in more than two years
squawks.detail: An economist reviewing the October flash PMI says the survey records the first increase in jobs in over two years. He adds that the employment balance is moving back into line with output growth.

squawks.headline: GfK links October slump in UK consumer confidence to the cost of living, inflation and Iran; morale and big-purchase gauges lead the fall
squawks.detail: The drop in GfK's UK consumer confidence index came mainly from its general economic outlook and major purchase components. A post noted that a fall this large has happened in only six months over the past 52 years.

squawks.headline: UK flash composite PMI climbs to 53.1 in October from 52.0, beating the 51.7 forecast; manufacturing rises to 52.8
squawks.detail: The October flash composite PMI came in at 53.1, against a forecast of 51.7 and 52.0 the previous month. The flash manufacturing PMI rose to 52.8 from 51.9, also above the 51.8 forecast.

squawks.headline: UK flash services PMI rises to 53.1 in October from 52.1, well above the 51.8 forecast
squawks.detail: The flash UK services PMI for October came in at 53.1, against a forecast of 51.8 and a previous reading of 52.1.

squawks.headline: Treasury minister Murray says UK fiscal rules support stability as the Budget comes amid global uncertainty
squawks.detail: Treasury minister Murray said the fiscal rules underpin the UK economy's stability and that the Budget comes during a period of unprecedented global economic instability. She added that the government is focused on entrepreneurs and on helping businesses grow.

squawks.headline: Iran says it has halted 'illicit' shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, Fars reports
squawks.detail: Iran says it has stopped vessel traffic in the Strait of Hormuz that it calls illicit, according to the Fars news agency. The report gives no further details and no market reaction has been reported.

squawks.headline: Brent hits $114 a barrel for the first time since May as AI worries weigh on global stocks, FT reports
squawks.detail: The FT reports oil has reached $114 a barrel for the first time since May, while global equities have been hit by concerns over the AI boom. European and US markets are reported to be steadier.

squawks.headline: BoJ sees rates still far from neutral and is expected to keep raising them quickly, with December in focus, sources say
squawks.detail: Sources say the Bank of Japan thinks inflation needs to settle near its target and that interest rates remain well short of neutral. The sources also say the central bank is expected to keep raising rates rapidly, with attention on December.

squawks.headline: ECB consumer survey shows 12-month inflation expectations rise to 3.1% in September; 3-year expectations stay at 2.9%
squawks.detail: The ECB's consumer expectations survey has 12-month-ahead inflation expectations at 3.1% in September, up from 3.0% in August. Expectations three years ahead are unchanged at 2.9%.

squawks.headline: Eurozone flash composite PMI falls to 51.9 in October from 53.1, short of the 52.7 forecast, with services at 51.7
squawks.detail: The eurozone flash services PMI fell to 51.7 from 53.0, against a 52.5 forecast. Flash manufacturing slipped to 52.4 from 52.9, below the 52.8 forecast.

squawks.headline: German flash composite PMI falls to 52.8 in October from 53.8 as services slip to 51.7, while manufacturing rises to 54.2
squawks.detail: Germany's October flash composite PMI came in at 52.8, below the 53.4 forecast, and services fell to 51.7 from 52.9 against a 52.5 forecast. Manufacturing beat expectations at 54.2, up from 53.9, with 53.5 forecast.

squawks.headline: French flash manufacturing PMI slips to 49.3 in October from 50.6 and the composite falls to 48.4, both short of forecasts
squawks.detail: S&P Global's October flash survey shows French manufacturing at 49.3 against a 50.5 forecast. The composite PMI came in at 48.4, below the expected 50.7, down from 51.2.

squawks.headline: French flash services PMI drops to 48.4 in October from 51.2, well below the 50.7 forecast
squawks.detail: France's October flash services PMI came in at 48.4, against a forecast of 50.7 and a previous reading of 51.2.

squawks.headline: China pledges to respond to US restrictions on research ties and demands an end to measures against its research bodies
squawks.detail: China's Commerce Ministry said it would take action after the US imposed curbs on research ties, and called on Washington to stop what it described as discriminatory measures against Chinese research institutions. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Tanker with 40,000 tonnes of Russian diesel heads for New York following a Putin-Trump agreement, Reuters reports
squawks.detail: Reuters reports, citing LSEG shipping data, that a Malta-flagged tanker carrying 40,000 metric tons of Russian diesel is bound for New York following an agreement with US President Trump.

squawks.headline: BoJ says Japanese banks can withstand stress from oil and AI risks, and flags energy costs squeezing SME profits
squawks.detail: The Bank of Japan's Financial Stability Report says higher raw material and energy prices appear to be weighing on profits, particularly at SMEs, and that some firms are relatively exposed to higher crude prices. It also says the Middle East situation, AI-related investment, non-bank developments, asset prices and growing concentration in private funds' portfolios all need close monitoring.

squawks.headline: BoJ Financial Stability Report finds Japan's financial system broadly stable, with no major imbalances
squawks.detail: The Bank of Japan published its latest Financial Stability Report, which judged the financial system broadly stable and found no major imbalances.

squawks.headline: UK retail sales fall 0.4% on the month in September, a bigger drop than the 0.1% forecast
squawks.detail: Including fuel, September retail sales fell 0.4% on the month after a 0.5% rise previously. Excluding fuel, annual growth was 0.8% against a 1.4% estimate and 2.7% previously.

squawks.headline: UK retail sales growth slows to 0.8% year on year, short of the 1% forecast, as core sales fall 0.7% on the month
squawks.detail: Official UK retail sales rose 0.8% year on year, below the 1% forecast and down from 2.4% previously. Core sales also grew 0.8% year on year against a 1.4% forecast and 2.7% previously, and fell 0.7% month on month against a forecast fall of 0.1% and a previous rise of 0.6%.

squawks.headline: Iran threatens wider attacks on economic and civilian sites in retaliation for US strike, WSJ reports
squawks.detail: The Wall Street Journal reports that Iran has warned it could widen its attacks to economic and civilian targets in response to a US strike. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Chancellor Healey to pledge cuts to paperwork for small UK firms, with savings put at £800mn a year, FT reports
squawks.detail: The Financial Times reports that the Chancellor will promise to remove unnecessary paperwork for small companies. The government says the deregulation drive could reduce business costs by £800mn a year.

squawks.headline: India's October flash composite PMI rises to 56.7 from 55.9 as services reach 56.2
squawks.detail: The HSBC flash composite PMI for India beat the 56.1 forecast, and services rose to 56.2 from 55.2 against a 55.5 forecast. Manufacturing slipped to 54.9 from 55.1, just below the 55.0 forecast.

squawks.headline: US envoy Waltz says the US can keep its Iran blockade in place for the foreseeable future and presses Tehran for a nuclear deal
squawks.detail: In an interview with the FT, Mike Waltz, US ambassador to the UN, said the US is ready for a long stand-off with Iran. He warned that Tehran must reach a meaningful agreement on its nuclear programme.

squawks.headline: Treasuries post their biggest daily rally in more than three years as a tech sell-off drives a move into safe havens
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that worries over the funding needs of AI hit technology stocks and pushed investors into sovereign bonds and safe-haven currencies, cutting bets on rate hikes. The FT reports the yen rallying as Asian stocks followed Wall Street lower.

squawks.headline: 2-year JGB yield falls 6bp to 1.840%
squawks.detail: Japan's 2-year government bond yield fell 6bp to 1.840% in Tokyo trade on Friday.

squawks.headline: PBOC sets yuan midpoint at 6.7180 per dollar, the strongest fixing since 2 February 2023
squawks.detail: The People's Bank of China set its daily yuan reference rate at 6.7180 per dollar. Market estimates had put the fixing at 6.6758.

squawks.headline: Japan's October flash manufacturing PMI falls to 53.3 from 54.1 while services rise to 52.0
squawks.detail: In S&P Global's October flash survey, Japan's composite PMI was unchanged at 52.3. The services PMI rose to 52.0 from 51.3.

squawks.headline: JGB yields fall in early Tokyo trade, with the 10-year down 7bp at 2.810%
squawks.detail: The 5-year JGB yield fell 8bp to 2.210% and the 20-year fell 6bp to 3.620%, while 10-year JGB futures gained 0.6 point. Asia-Pacific equities opened lower amid moves into safe-haven assets.

squawks.headline: UK grid operators expect adequate gas and electricity supply this winter, with peak gas supply at 592 mcm
squawks.detail: Britain's energy grid operators project that peak daily gas demand this winter will be 493 mcm, against peak supply of 592 mcm. They expect electricity supply to be sufficient.

squawks.headline: US has strike plans against Iran ready with Israel, including energy facilities, CNN reports citing US officials
squawks.detail: CNN, citing US officials, reports that Trump's advisers have drawn up plans for strikes on Iran coordinated with Israel that could proceed as soon as he approves. Targets would include nuclear infrastructure, missile and drone depots and energy facilities, and the officials say using the largest US conventional bomb is one option under consideration.

squawks.headline: US Treasury proposes tighter curbs on investment in sensitive Chinese technology, FT reports
squawks.detail: According to the FT, the proposed restrictions would cover investment in areas including AI, hypersonic weapons and biotech.

squawks.headline: Japan's September core CPI rises to 2.1% year on year from 1.7%, matching forecasts
squawks.detail: Japanese government data show headline CPI at 2.1% against 1.9% previously, and the measure excluding fresh food and energy at 2.4%. Reports say core inflation is above 2% for the first time since December 2023.

squawks.headline: Chancellor Healey says next week's Budget will target entrepreneurs, FT reports
squawks.detail: The FT reports that the Chancellor intends to aim next week's Budget at entrepreneurs, as the number of UK founders choosing to sell their businesses rather than scale them reaches an eight-year high.

squawks.headline: UK GfK consumer confidence drops to -24 in October from -13, its biggest monthly fall since 2020
squawks.detail: GfK's October survey shows the major purchases index at its lowest since September 2024, while the inflation outlook component rose.

squawks.headline: Australia's October flash composite PMI drops to 47.7 from 51.3 as services fall to 47.8
squawks.detail: S&P Global's flash readings show the services PMI down to 47.8 from 51.9, while manufacturing edged up to 49.7 from 49.6.

squawks.headline: UK banking watchdog to review how financial regulation affects investment, capital and growth, Reuters reports
squawks.detail: Reuters reports that the new UK banking watchdog will examine the effect of its rules on competitiveness, with more focus on transparency and on an objective to promote competition.

squawks.headline: Trump invokes the Defense Production Act to expand US petroleum capacity
squawks.detail: The US president invoked the Defense Production Act for petroleum capacity, waived the Act's section 303 rules to expand oil capacity and sent a memo on the matter to Defense Secretary Hegseth, according to market news posts.

squawks.headline: Trump warns the US may carry out further strikes on Iran
squawks.detail: US President Trump says the US has already struck Iran hard and may strike again. No market reaction was reported in the posts.

squawks.headline: UK relaxes 'fit and proper' rules for holding bankers to account, FT reports
squawks.detail: The Financial Times reports that the UK is loosening the regulatory regime that requires bankers to be fit and proper. The regime was central to past actions against former Barclays chief executive Jes Staley and hedge fund owner Crispin Odey.

squawks.headline: Trump executive order directs US trade negotiations on wind turbine imports
squawks.detail: A White House executive order released on Thursday tells the Commerce Secretary and the US Trade Representative to pursue negotiations on wind turbine imports, Reuters reports. They must report back to the President on progress within 180 days.

squawks.headline: Russia agrees to resume trilateral peace talks with the US and Ukraine, with technical talks possibly in Abu Dhabi in mid-November
squawks.detail: The agreement came during a visit by US envoy Steve Witkoff, who also secured the release of US detainee Stephen Hubbard and discussed Russian diesel shipments, according to a market news account. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Trump signs executive order on US housing costs that seeks to cut mortgage insurance premiums
squawks.detail: The White House says President Trump has signed an executive order aimed at lowering housing costs for Americans. Reports say the order seeks to reduce mortgage insurance premiums.

squawks.headline: Romanian president says Russia looks more focused on escalating the Ukraine war than on pursuing peace
squawks.detail: Romania's President Nicușor Dan questioned whether Moscow is ready for a deal despite US-led diplomacy. He urged NATO members to raise their readiness while avoiding further escalation, as EU members prepare for possible Russian hybrid threats.

squawks.headline: UK Chancellor plans to cut back business asset disposal relief, Telegraph reports
squawks.detail: The Telegraph reports that the Chancellor is set to scale back business asset disposal relief. No further details or figures were given.

squawks.headline: Lebanon-Israel talks in Florida end with no breakthrough, US official says
squawks.detail: A US official told Al Arabiya that the meetings in Florida between Lebanon and Israel ended without a breakthrough. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Brent crude futures settle 4.00% higher at $113.17 a barrel, up $4.35
squawks.detail: Brent futures closed the session $4.35, or 4.00%, higher at $113.17 a barrel, after Houthi attacks earlier in the day raised fears over Middle East supply.

squawks.headline: Putin says trilateral talks with the US and Ukraine will cover Russian and Ukrainian security, and European security too
squawks.detail: Russia's president said the planned trilateral talks involving the US and Ukraine would focus on security guarantees for Russia and Ukraine. He added that European security should also be on the agenda.

squawks.headline: Putin says Russia has no plans to go to war with Europe
squawks.detail: The Russian president said Russia does not plan to wage war on Europe, according to a wire headline.

squawks.headline: WTI crude settles up 2.39% at $99.47 a barrel
squawks.detail: NYMEX December WTI futures settled $2.32 higher at $99.47 a barrel. November diesel futures settled at $4.9321 a gallon and November gasoline at $3.1765 a gallon.

squawks.headline: Putin describes eastern Ukraine as historically Russian territory
squawks.detail: Russian President Vladimir Putin made the remark about eastern Ukraine. Ukraine has said it is ready for peace talks, and the Kremlin has not yet named its representative for trilateral talks with the US and Ukraine.

squawks.headline: Egypt urges talks on Yemen as its parliament prepares to vote on military support for Saudi Arabia against the Houthis
squawks.detail: Egypt's foreign minister said Cairo favours pursuing every diplomatic option to end the Yemen conflict, Reuters reports. The parliament votes next week on whether to authorise the armed forces to support Saudi Arabia against the Iran-aligned Houthis.

squawks.headline: Canada's chief negotiator on US trade says tariff-free trade with the US is not expected to return
squawks.detail: Canada's US trade negotiator, Charette, said Canada should not expect a return to tariff-free trade with the United States. No market reaction was reported.

squawks.headline: Brent extends its rally to a $4 a barrel gain, hitting a five-month high as Houthi attacks raise Middle East supply fears
squawks.detail: Oil futures pushed further ahead late on Thursday, with Brent crude up $4 a barrel on the day at a five-month high. The rise is reported to be driven by worries over Middle East supply after Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia.

squawks.headline: Finland's prime minister rules out gas deals with Russia while the war continues
squawks.detail: Finland's prime minister said there can be no gas deals with Russia for as long as the war in Ukraine goes on.

squawks.headline: Zelenskiy says Ukraine is ready for peace talks at the G20 but has had no invitation so far
squawks.detail: Ukraine's President Zelenskiy said Kyiv is prepared to hold peace talks at the G20 and has not yet been invited. He also said he hopes to discuss Starlink with US Secretary of State Rubio in the coming days.

squawks.headline: Rubio reaffirms US commitment to Qatar's security and to freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz
squawks.detail: The US State Department says Secretary of State Rubio restated US support for Qatar's security and for free passage through the Strait of Hormuz. The readout refers to Qatar's prime minister and foreign minister, Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani.

squawks.headline: US $26bn 5-year TIPS auction tails 0.7bp at 2.367% high yield, bid-to-cover 2.41
squawks.detail: The US Treasury sold $26bn of 5-year TIPS at a high yield of 2.367%, against a when-issued level of about 2.36% before the sale, with bid-to-cover at 2.41. Indirect bidders took 62.0%, direct bidders 32.4% and primary dealers 5.5%.

squawks.headline: Traders stop fully pricing a Fed rate hike before the end of 2026
squawks.detail: Market commentary reports that money markets no longer fully price a Federal Reserve rate increase before year-end, as the US Treasury rally continues.

squawks.headline: Senior Israeli officers see no reason to strike Iran ahead of the US elections, Ynet reports
squawks.detail: Israeli outlet Ynet reports that senior Israeli military officers see no reason for a strike on Iran before the US elections. No market reaction was reported.
